terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: The sheet contains several independently framed concept views, so no single photographic camera solve applies. Match the hero panel with an approximate 38-degree perspective camera and validate the other views independently.

objectClass.notes: A standalone static vehicle with no puller, carrier, skin, or baked animation. The rider is composed by the existing mount system onto Socket_Rider. Runtime motion and exhaust belong in the sled's own render module.

reasoning: The core silhouette is simple, but twin rockets, runner assemblies, seat structure, tank, pipes, brackets, bands, caps, and fins create a deep mechanical hierarchy.
Rivet rows, tank bands, cushion panels, plank seams, mirrored runners, and mirrored rockets require explicit repetition systems.
The concept sheet provides hero, front, side, rear, top, and three-quarter views, so most visible structure can be resolved without inventing a hidden-side design.
The chase-camera mount role makes material separation, rider clearance, effect sockets, and stable runtime pivots part of the quality bar.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The vehicle reads through nested mechanical assemblies and repeated hardware, not through one primary mass.

detailInventory.note: The 4x4 scan covered the full concept sheet. Details below map to planned component localFeatures or material localOverrides in the sculpt spec.

details.description: Both long runners terminate in a shallow upward curve with a reinforced dark-metal nose cap.
Regular raised rivets follow both runner edge straps from the front tips toward the chassis.
Longitudinal timber planks and dark gaps create the deck's main surface rhythm.
Chunky iron angle brackets overlap the deck and runner frame at corners and cross-members.
Raised rivets repeat around each rocket's segmented barrel bands.
Concentric stepped rings form each rear nozzle and frame the glowing exhaust core.
A hot orange core sits inside each dark nozzle with a brighter center and darker rim.
Triangular red fins interrupt the rear side silhouette of both rocket bodies.
The central tank is divided by multiple wide dark iron bands with riveted faces.
Two top caps and smaller valve hardware project above the low tank profile.
Bent dark pipes run from the central tank toward the two rocket mounts.
Seat and backrest use segmented red-brown leather pads with recessed seams and button-like dimples.
Red painted steel shows directional scratches and chipped edges exposing dark metal.
Dark iron bands and brackets carry warm rust in rivet cavities and overlaps.
White skull-and-bones markings conform to both side rocket barrels without readable text or tangent-plane protrusion.
A green goblin skull mask with red eyes and dark spikes anchors the sled's front center.

anatomy.note: Not applicable to a standalone vehicle.

definitionOfDone: The vehicle reads immediately as the concept's low, wide goblin rocket sled from hero, front, profile, rear, and gameplay chase-camera views.
Twin side rockets, long upturned runners, the open tufted seat, low central tank, and front goblin-face ornament preserve the concept's identity and proportions.
The rider socket preserves head, shoulder, arm, and leg clearance without adding handlebars or controls absent from the concept.
Worn red paint, dark iron, wood, leather, bone, and orange exhaust remain distinct under Standard and Low-tier material paths.
The shipped vehicle stays within the locked triangle, byte, primitive, and material budgets, with no skin or baked animation.
Runtime-only bob, slope tilt, exhaust flicker, and held rocket loop reset correctly on dismount and do not mutate the shared cached asset.

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed if a required feature group lacks component, material, or runtime representation.
Do not proceed if any connector, pipe, fin, mount, or ornament lacks an explicit attachment contract.
Do not use baked animation for bob, tilt, or exhaust flicker.
Do not alias albedo into normal, roughness, metalness, or occlusion channels.
Do not treat painted lighting in the AI concept as ground-truth PBR evidence.
Do not proceed if runner, rocket, seat, or tank proportions fail a critical comparison view.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The source is user-supplied AI concept art generated with GPT; exact model, prompt, and timestamp were not supplied and are not invented here.

featureReviews.notes: Both rockets visibly carry matched barrel bands, outward rivets, conical noses, stepped dark nozzles, emissive cores, mirrored fins, supported mounts, and buried fuel lines.

The runtime-normalized shipped knight in Sit_Floor_Idle remains centered between the rockets; per-mesh AABB checks report false for both rockets and the tank, and the seat rails remain below the hands and elbows in hero and top captures.

featureReviews.notes: The 3.8-deep runners, central open deck, rear tank, compact seat, and low mirrored rockets preserve the concept's distinctive vehicle silhouette in hero, front, side, rear, and top views.
The paired rocket systems retain matched conical noses, four-band rhythm, fasteners, stepped nozzles, glow cores, supported mounts, fuel lines, and reduced mirrored fins.

The prow now reads as a goblin skull through a backed cranium, angled brows, glowing eyes, ears, nose, jaw, mouth cavity, fangs, cheek horns, and backing spikes; rocket plaques, tuft buttons, brackets, pipes, planks, and rivets carry the same ramshackle language.

featureReviews.notes: Red paint, dark iron, wood, leather, off-white plaques, green bone, and orange glow remain distinct. Nine independent 1024px albedo/normal/ORM maps show metal scratches and chips, directional wood grain and seams, and quilted leather relief; nozzle cores remain bounded and readable.

visualEvidence.notes: gltf-transform inspection confirms six materials, nine 1024x1024 WebP textures, COLOR_0 plus TEXCOORD_0 on mapped geometry, no skins, and no animations. Raw authoring asset remains 5671 triangles.

featureReviews.notes: Baked cavity/contact shading reinforces the attached bands, brackets, rivets, pipe roots, plank seams, tuft buttons, skull planes, and runner contacts without obscuring their hierarchy.

Grazing light shows tactile metal, wood, and leather response without noisy tiling. Rear-only soot and runner-underside contact wear are localized in vertex color, while the symmetric nozzle cores remain bounded and clear.

The prow now reads as a goblin skull through a backed cranium, angled brows, glowing eyes, ears, nose, jaw, mouth cavity, fangs, cheek horns, and backing spikes; rocket plaques, tuft buttons, brackets, pipes, planks, and rivets carry the same ramshackle language.

performanceBudget.budgetBasis: Ordinary shipped mounts range from 1,854 to 5,000 triangles, the current Bonebound Rickshaw build uses 2,732, and the premium Terrorspark Groundshaker uses 12,448. This sled may spend above the ordinary range for premium close-camera detail, but must remain below Terrorspark.
performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Aim for 6,500 triangles. Preserve runners, rocket ring rhythm, rider clearance, tank, goblin ornament, and material separation. Any build above 8,000 triangles needs a visual comparison showing which identity-critical geometry earns the premium cost. Never exceed 12,000. Instance repeated hardware, merge by six material buckets, and share three procedural PBR map families.

lightingFromPhoto: Key light: broad warm front-left key at about 35 degrees elevation, used only to compare shape hierarchy.
Fill light: cool right-side fill that keeps runner undersides, rocket mounts, and seat frame readable.
Rim or environment light: restrained rear-right cool rim separating tank valves, fins, and exhaust nozzles.
Review exposure 1.0 with ACES tone mapping, neutral blue-gray background, soft contact shadow, plus a separate grazing-light material proof.
proceduralStrategy: Author a purpose-built deterministic scripts/assets/goblin_rocket_sled/model.js factory from named primitive and profile systems.
Use semantic vertex colors for macro shading and three independent procedural PBR map families for metal, wood, and leather.
Use world-space box-projected UVs, fold repeats into quantizable range, and restore scale through KHR_texture_transform.
Merge static geometry by six material buckets while retaining stable named nodes and sockets required at runtime.
Drive bob, slope tilt, exhaust flicker, and held-loop audio from src/render/goblin_rocket_sled.ts, never renderer.ts or baked animation.
Run KTX2 compression after every exporter pass and regenerate the media manifest.
animationAnchors: Socket_Rider: existing player mount attachment point above the seat cushion.
Socket_Exhaust_L and Socket_Exhaust_R: pooled runtime flame and smoke origins inside the rear nozzles.
Root_SledMotion: allocation-free procedural bob and slope-tilt transform owned by the sled render module.
destructionAnchors: No destruction ships this pass; component hierarchy preserves future detachable rocket, runner, and tank seams without exposing runtime break behavior.
risks: The dense concept can turn into noisy primitive clutter; each pass must preserve the macro hierarchy before adding rivets.
The rider can clip the tank or side rockets if the seat is scaled from the illustration without live-rig proof.
Nine embedded maps can exceed the byte ceiling unless resolutions and channel frequencies are tuned before KTX2 compression.
Runtime exhaust or bloom can obscure the sled and nearby gameplay; effects remain cosmetic, pooled, and bounded.
Shared mount, audio, content, i18n, icon, and Reliquary files require explicit user approval before modification.
